body_markdown:
Free image via[Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/ZtI4l8EvyUw)


Libraries are a precious resource. They’ve helped advance culture and knowledge for thousands of years. They’ve moved from ancient archives of the written word to sources of free multi-media information. You might say they, and the knowledge they hold, are made to keep.


Part community gathering grounds, part educational mecca, part architectural wonder, libraries often reflect the heart and soul of a city better than anything else. They serve as safe spaces, lead conversations on human rights, provide thoughtful assistance, organize learning events, and give access to digital resources.


We’ve chosen to explore some of the best libraries in the U.S. that not only do all the above but go beyond. From unique events to rare books, a multitude of services to community involvement, these libraries represent and help shape the values of the cities they serve. Each one deserves to be cherished, preserved, and celebrated.


## 1.[San Diego Public Library](https://www.sandiego.gov/public-library) , San Diego, CA


Free Image via[Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/wooden-ladder-by-bookshelves-1JBOZwuW7sI)


With[San Diego Central Library](https://www.sandiego.gov/public-library/central-library) at the core, this system of libraries serves the many neighborhoods of the sprawling city, with 36 branches. The central library opened in its new location in 2013, a nine-story building that houses a charter high school, innovation lab with free computer classes, an art gallery, and the OliverMcMillan I Can! Center for patrons with disabilities. And the community love shows, too. Support from groups like[Friends of San Diego Library](https://friendsofsandiegocentrallibrary.org/) help fulfill their mission: To inspire lifelong learning through connections to knowledge and each other.


**Other notable San Diego libraries**
The[San Diego State University Library](https://library.sdsu.edu/) is architecturally stunning and has an impressive collection and resource center.


## 2.[Kansas City Public Library](https://kclibrary.org/) **, Kansas City, MO**


Free Image via[Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/books-on-brown-wooden-shelf-Ft_Wn-K5YH8)


The[Kansas City Central](https://kclibrary.org/library-locations/central-library)[Library](https://kclibrary.org/library-locations/central-library) stands out with its giant “bookshelf” parking garage, featuring 25-foot-tall book spines. This library has won various awards, including consistent 5-star ratings from the “Library Journal.” It’s easy to see why. They host events like ESL classes, storytimes, film screenings, and have study rooms and an in-house café where patrons meet and share ideas. This group of 10 branches has multiple programs like the Community Reference Team, which connects people with resources to find jobs, start businesses, grow nonprofits, and manage personal finances. Now that’s taking care of business.


**Other notable Kansas City libraries**
The[Mid-Continent Public Library](https://www.mymcpl.org/) system comprises 31 branches, including some in Kansas City, and serves about 840,000 people in over 1,400 square miles in three counties, 56 cities, and 21 school districts. They have an extensive collection, inter-library loaning, online classes, and lots of educational and fun events. The Midwest Genealogy Center houses nearly 750,000 on-site print and digital genealogy resources. Its collections include volumes on family histories, print volumes like year books, oral histories, city directories, and local histories.


## 3.[New York Public Library](https://www.nypl.org/) , New York, NY


Free Image via[Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/interior-building-OvXht_wi5Ew)


One of the most-visited public libraries in the world,[New York Public Library](https://www.nypl.org/) is at the forefront of what libraries can do. From the beautiful Stephen A. Schwarzman Building, famously featured in many movies and TV shows, to other distinguished sites like the[Jefferson Market Library](https://www.nypl.org/locations/jefferson-market) and[Yorkville](https://www.nypl.org/locations/yorkville) , this world-renowned library system includes four major research libraries and 92 branches. The children’s center is home to the real Winnie-the-Pooh and friends, and the calendar of free events, including those of the Library for the Performing Arts, is packed year-round.


**Other notable New York libraries**
Don’t ignore the[Brooklyn Public Library](https://www.bklynlibrary.org/locations/central) , which is also one of the most-visited in the world and is a breathtaking Art Deco experience. Independently run[Poets House](https://poetshouse.org/) is a love letter to the genre and a must for any aspiring poet.


## 4.[District of Columbia Public Library](https://www.dclibrary.org/) , Washington, D.C.


Free Image via[Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/grand-library-interior-with-ornate-architecture-and-reading-desks-rLfe8e3L44k)


The Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Library’s People Archive includes several notable collections, including the “Washington Star” Photograph Collection, which contains approximately 1.3 million photographs, and the Black Studies Center Collection, which preserves documents and other materials related to Black history and culture. It’s also home to a 3D printer and the Espresso Book Machine, which collates, covers, and binds a single book in a matter of minutes. Neighborhood branches include architecturally distinctive[Francis A. Gregory Neighborhood Library](https://www.dclibrary.org/francis) .


**Other notable D.C. libraries**
Though the[Library of Congress](https://www.loc.gov/) is open to the public, only some government officials and library employees may check out books and materials. However, as the de facto national library of the United States, its importance is clear. The symbolic art and architecture alone are worth a visit.


## 5.[Seattle Public Library](https://www.spl.org/) , Seattle, WA


Free Image via[Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/white-concrete-building-RT3pJdcnI4Q)


The principal branch in this system is the Central Library with its ultra-modern steel and glass exterior. Unique to this structure is the four-story-high Books Spiral, where patrons can peruse the whole nonfiction collection without using stairs. There are 26 branches in the system, with programs that include free passes to local museums, kid’s storytime, job resources, personal reading recommendations, and free writing and publishing classes.


**Other notable Seattle libraries**
Visually impaired patrons and others unable to read standard print materials are a top priority at the award-winning[Washington Talking Book & Braille Library](https://www.wtbbl.org/) , in operation since 1931.[University of Washington Libraries](https://www.lib.washington.edu/) system is one of the largest academic research libraries in North America and has been honored with the Association of College and Research Libraries Excellence in Academic Libraries award.


## 6.[Free Library of Philadelphia](http://www.freelibrary.org/) , Philadelphia, PA


Free Image via[Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/a-library-filled-with-lots-of-books-and-people-ilgDsWkFBaw)


The worthy mission, “To advance literacy, guide learning, and inspire curiosity,” guides this system of libraries. Its Parkway Central Library has been doing as much since 1927 and greets visitors in grand Parisian Beaux-Arts style. Areas like the Marie and Joseph Field Teen Center and the Robert and Eileen Kennedy Heim Center for Cultural and Civic Engagement were designed to promote engagement, interaction, and discourse. It has also had measurable community impact, with one study showing it helped nearly 25,000 people learn to read or teach someone else to read.


**Other notable Philadelphia libraries**
Housed in a National Historic Landmark,[The Athenaeum of Philadelphia](http://www.philaathenaeum.org/) specializes in architecture and interior design history and contains a museum collection of early-to-mid 19th-century American arts.


## 7.[Ann Arbor District Library](https://aadl.org/) , Ann Arbor, MI


Free Image via[Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/photo-of-brown-wooden-bookshelf-xrbbXIXAWY0)


The Ann Arbor District Library has earned Library Journal’s highest 5-star rating every year since the America’s Star Libraries rankings began in 2008, making it one of the nation’s most highly regarded public library systems. The main Downtown Library in Ann Arbor has been in operation since 1957, and has a local history section, genealogy reference materials, a large folklore and fairytales collection, as well as various electronic resources. AADL events include film screenings, gaming nights, poetry readings, storytimes, workshops, and crafts.


**Other notable Ann Arbor libraries**
As the third-largest research library in the U.S.,[University of Michigan Library](https://www.lib.umich.edu/) is consistently ranked in the top 10 by the Association of Research Libraries.


## 8.[Boston Public Library](https://www.bpl.org/) , Boston, MA


Free Image via[Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/hand-reaching-for-books-on-shelf-B30XL_m3fso)


Home to the third-largest public library in the United States, the city of Boston enjoys riches beyond most book lovers’ dreams.[Boston Central Library](https://www.bpl.org/locations/3/) in Copley Square is headquarters to the 24 branches in the system, and the reading room in the McKim Building would turn anyone studious. The libraries host thousands of free programs every year, including author talks, concerts, daily children’s events, and therapy dog storytimes.


**Other notable Boston libraries**
The[John F. Kennedy Presidential Library & Museum](https://www.jfklibrary.org/) holds permanent collections like the gifts from heads of state in the White House Corridor and the Ernest Hemingway Collection, which features his personal papers. And then there’s nearby[Harvard Library](https://library.harvard.edu/) , the oldest library system in the U.S., which needs zero introduction.


## 9.[Chicago Public Library](https://www.chipublib.org/) , Chicago, IL


Free image via[Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/9BoqXzEeQqM)


The American Library Association is headquartered in Chicago, so you know this city likes to read. The CPL, which boasts 81 locations and some of the best public libraries in the U.S., includes the central library,[Harold Washington Library Center](https://www.chipublib.org/locations/34/) . There, the ninth-floor Winter Garden is a beautifully unique feature, and the Maker Lab includes multiple 3D printers, CNC machines, and laser cutters. It’s also the largest public library in the U.S. to eliminate fines for overdue items, forgiving all existing fees. Services include a free lecture series, the Words and Music Program, and free homework help.


**Other notable Chicago libraries**
[The Newberry Library](https://www.newberry.org/) is an independent research library with materials spanning over six centuries, and the[University of Chicago Library](https://www.lib.uchicago.edu/) is the tenth-largest academic library in North America. Chicago is also home to the[Barack Obama Presidential Center](https://www.obama.org/the-center/) , which includes a branch of the CPL.


## 10.[Hennepin County Library,](https://www.hclib.org/) Minneapolis, MN


Free Image via[Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/assorted-title-book-lot-eeSdJfLfx1A)


This network is a vast library system with 41 locations, including impressive suburban libraries with art collections, outreach services for at-home patrons, and other innovative programs. Its largest location, the[Minneapolis Central Library](https://www.hclib.org/about/locations/minneapolis-central) , features special historical collections, technology labs, gallery art, a piano room, and energy efficiencies, including a roof garden and substantial daylight. Partially supported by groups like[Friends of the Hennepin County Library](https://www.supporthclib.org/) , these branches are essential parts of their communities and the county as a whole.


**Other notable Minneapolis libraries**
Featuring some of the most distinctive research collections in the country, the[University of Minnesota Libraries](https://www.lib.umn.edu/) are a destination for scholars, students, and lifelong learners alike. At the heart of its Archives and Special Collections is the renowned Sherlock Holmes Collections, widely recognized as the world’s largest gathering of materials related to Sherlock Holmes and creator Sir Arthur Conan Doyle. Spanning more than 60,000 items, including rare books, manuscripts, journals, artwork, memorabilia, and digital resources, the collection attracts researchers and enthusiasts from around the globe.


## 11.[McAllen Public Library](https://mcallenlibrary.net/) , McAllen, TX


Free Image via[Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/photo-of-library-with-turned-on-lights-sfL_QOnmy00)


When Walmart moved out, the library moved in to become the largest single-floor library in the United States. This remarkable place wins awards for online presence, architecture, services, and believes in “free access to information that connects a culturally diverse population with the global community.” Though a small system, these libraries receive rave reviews, and events like the South Texas Book Festival and regular programs bring the community together through the power of books.


**Other notable McAllen libraries**
The[Hidalgo County Library System](https://hclstx.org/) has 12 members that coordinate to provide services to all area residents, with digital and physical resources.
